scenes.headline: How one photo becomes a camera move
scenes.sub: Exact cameras in, generated frames out
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Dolly! This app turns one photo into a four second camera move. You might expect a 3D world behind it. There isn't one.

scenes.text: The app never renders a 3D scene. It computes 48 exact cameras from your path, and a world model paints a frame at each one.
scenes.mark: a world model paints a frame at each one
scenes.say: The app never renders a scene. It works out forty-eight exact cameras, and a world model paints one frame at each camera.

scenes.title: From a photo to forty-eight frames

steps.say: One photo goes to World Labs and comes back with an estimated camera and a depth map.
Your browser lifts every pixel out to its depth. That point cloud is only a preview.
You click a few keyframes over it and choose where the camera looks.
A smooth curve through those keys is sampled into forty-eight exact cameras.
Atlas gets the photo, its depth and those cameras, and paints a frame for each.

scenes.title: Every section gets equal time
scenes.text: frame of key k = round(47 k / S)

parts.say: Keyframe k of S sections lands at that share of the clip, however long the section is.

scenes.label: speed jump when one section is short and the next is long
scenes.note: the uneven preset in the article's editor
scenes.say: So a short section then a long one crawls, then lunges. In the uneven example, the fastest step is seventeen point seven times the slowest.

steps.say: Here is the repository's fish orbit, seen from the side.
By frame thirty-three the camera is underneath it. Nobody photographed that side. The model invented it.

left.title: Splat flythrough
left.say: A splat flythrough shows only what was rebuilt, as long as you like, the same every time.

right.title: Atlas shot
items: Fills what the photo never saw
right.say: An Atlas shot fills in what the photo never saw. It is short, it costs money, and every seed differs.

scenes.text: The camera is exact because it is just geometry. What appears in the frame is entirely the model's.
scenes.say: The camera is exact, because it is just geometry. What appears in the frame is entirely the model's.
One photo, a drawn path, forty-eight cameras, and a model that paints the rest.
